name: TabView raw content assignment
description: TabView does NOT stretch child controls vertically. Setting .Content = new TextBox() will render the control at its natural height (~50px) instead of filling the tab area.
fix: Use a Frame per tab and navigate to Page types: var frame = new Frame(); frame.Navigate(typeof(EditorPage)); tab.Content = frame; — or scaffold with 'dotnet new winui-tabview'. Alternative: place a shared editor Grid in a separate Grid row below the TabView strip.

name: WebView2 NavigateToString without init
description: Calling NavigateToString() or accessing CoreWebView2 before EnsureCoreWebView2Async() silently fails — nothing renders.

cross_file_check.message: No EnsureCoreWebView2Async() call found. WebView2 must be initialized before use.

fix: Add: await myWebView.EnsureCoreWebView2Async(); before any CoreWebView2 access. Use the CoreWebView2Initialized event for post-init setup.

name: UWP XAML namespace
description: Windows.UI.Xaml is the UWP namespace. WinUI 3 uses Microsoft.UI.Xaml.

name: Window.Current usage
description: Window.Current does not exist in WinUI 3 desktop apps. It is a UWP-only API.
fix: Store the window reference in App.xaml.cs: public static Window MainWindow { get; private set; } and use App.MainWindow instead.

name: CoreDispatcher usage
description: CoreDispatcher is UWP-only. WinUI 3 uses DispatcherQueue.
fix: Replace CoreDispatcher with DispatcherQueue. Use DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue() instead of Dispatcher.RunAsync().

name: GetForCurrentView UWP pattern
description: GetForCurrentView() is a UWP-only pattern. Desktop WinUI 3 apps must use HWND-based interop.
fix: Use HWND-based COM interop instead. See: https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/winrt-com-interop-csharp

name: Nested x:Bind without FallbackValue
description: Nested x:Bind paths like {x:Bind ViewModel.Selected.Name} crash with NullReferenceException if any segment is null at startup.
fix: Use a flat ViewModel property with null-safe getter: public string SelectedName => Selected?.Name ?? ""; — or add FallbackValue={x:Null} to the binding.

name: Old MVVM field-backed ObservableProperty
description: Field-backed [ObservableProperty] is the old CommunityToolkit.Mvvm 8.2 syntax. It generates AOT warnings (MVVMTK0045).
fix: Use partial property syntax: [ObservableProperty] public partial string Title { get; set; }

name: ObservableCollection replacement
description: Replacing an ObservableCollection instance breaks existing bindings silently. The UI stops updating.
fix: Never replace the collection. Use .Clear() + re-add items, or use collection.ReplaceRange() if available.

name: Interactive control missing AutomationId
description: Interactive controls without AutomationProperties.AutomationId make UI automation unreliable — slugs change on every re-render.
fix: Add AutomationProperties.AutomationId="BtnName" to every interactive control. Use PascalCase with type prefix: BtnSave, TxtSearch, CmbSize.

name: x:Bind without Mode
description: x:Bind defaults to Mode=OneTime — the UI will never update after initial load. This causes blank/stale UI.
fix: Add Mode=OneWay (or Mode=TwoWay for inputs): {x:Bind ViewModel.Title, Mode=OneWay}

name: TextChanged without update guard
description: TextChanged fires asynchronously when text is set programmatically, causing false dirty flags and infinite update loops.

cross_file_check.message: No update guard found. TextChanged handlers should check a guard flag to prevent re-entrant updates.

fix: Add a guard: private bool _isUpdating; — In the handler: if (_isUpdating) return; — Before programmatic updates: _isUpdating = true; textBox.Text = value; _isUpdating = false;

name: WebView2 in XAML without init in code-behind
description: XAML declares a WebView2 control but the code-behind has no EnsureCoreWebView2Async() call.
fix: Add to your initialization: await myWebView.EnsureCoreWebView2Async(); — typically in Loaded event or constructor after InitializeComponent().

name: TabView in XAML with raw content in code-behind
description: XAML has a TabView but code-behind assigns raw controls as tab content instead of using Frame+Page.
fix: Use Frame per tab: var frame = new Frame(); frame.Navigate(typeof(MyPage)); tab.Content = frame; — or scaffold with 'dotnet new winui-tabview'.
